title: Routing Policy Testbench — traffic replay, assertion rules, and fallback variant preview
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a Routing Policy Testbench to the Console: a first-class workflow where customers can replay a sample of production traffic against a candidate routing policy, assert expected outcomes, and preview fallback behavior when regions or model variants are unavailable. The objective is to reduce rollout risk by enabling deterministic, repeatable tests in the console before policy activation. The Testbench should accept recorded request traces or synthetic traffic templates, run them through the policy engine with configurable environment constraints (region outage, capacity tier throttle, model variant unavailability), and produce a per-request outcome log, metric diffs, and a human-readable explanation for why each request took its final route.
acceptance_criteria: Console adds a 'Testbench' tab in the Routing Policy editor where users can upload a traffic CSV/JSON or pick from saved sample traces.
Testbench can run simulations with environment toggles: region down, tier capacity reduced, and model variant unavailable; results show per-request decisions and fallback chain used.

Users can define assertion rules (e.g., >95% requests must hit region-us-east, model variant must not downgrade below 'gptx-quant') and the Testbench returns pass/fail with highlighted failing requests.
Telemetry dashboard links are available post-run showing estimated latency/cost delta vs baseline for the simulated policy change.
Engineering accepts the design and implements a feature flag guarded rollout with unit/integration tests and a performance budget for large traces (max 10k requests per run).

open_questions: What retention policy do we apply to uploaded traces? (GDPR/PII concerns)
Should assertions support percentile thresholds (p95 latency) in addition to route percentage checks?
Do we allow saving Testbench runs as named experiments for audit and drift tracking?
What quota limits should we enforce per-org for simulation runs to avoid heavy cost/compute usage?
next_steps: ENG: Create infra ticket ENG-89200 for model-variant compatibility API and quota enforcement (owner: Priya).
DES: Finalize microcopy for failure explanations and per-request reasoning (owner: Mei).
PM: Draft rollout plan and communications, including a recommended checklist for customers to run before policy activation (owner: Ava).
Set feature-flagged alpha for a subset of Beta orgs by 2026-02-18 and collect feedback from two pilot customers.
notes: Implementation must avoid executing live model inference. The simulation uses routing logic only and synthetic latency/cost models derived from per-model profiles in the catalog.
Telemetry should estimate cost delta using token-per-request multipliers and not actual billed usage to protect customer privacy and billing stability.
Add a developer-facing API (future work) to allow programmatic playback for CI workflows.
